name: Acadia National Park
signature: Cadillac Mountain summit, the first place in the U.S. to see sunrise from early October to early March
bestMonths: June and September to mid-October (fall foliage)
visitsNote: NPS 2024 figure as reported by Smithsonian (ranked 7th among national parks). One secondary list shows 4,079,318, which is probably a different year.

name: National Park of American Samoa
signature: Ofu Beach's coral reef lagoon, plus paleotropical rainforest with flying foxes (fruit bats) that have 3-foot wingspans
visitsNote: No 2024 figure turned up within the search budget. It is consistently one of the least-visited national parks, typically well under 20,000 a year (approximate, unverified).

name: Arches National Park
signature: Delicate Arch, the free-standing arch on Utah's license plate
bestMonths: March to May and September to October
visitsNote: From a secondary 2024 ranking list (explorewithalec) that draws on NPS stats. It was not checked directly against irma.nps.gov.

name: Badlands National Park
signature: The Badlands Wall: striped buttes and pinnacles along the Badlands Loop Road (SD-240)
bestMonths: May to June and September to October
visitsNote: No confirmed 2024 NPS figure. One secondary list (camperchamp, updated 2026) shows 1,139,361, but its year looks inconsistent (its Acadia number does not match NPS 2024). About 1.0 million in 2023 (approximate).

name: Big Bend National Park
signature: Santa Elena Canyon, with 1,500-foot limestone walls rising straight up from the Rio Grande
bestMonths: November to April (best in February to April)
visitsNote: From a secondary 2024 list (explorewithalec). The Daily Texan reported more than 560,000 visits in 2024, the park's second-highest year. Another list shows 568,104.

name: Biscayne National Park
signature: The Maritime Heritage Trail, an underwater trail of shipwrecks, plus the Boca Chita Key lighthouse
bestMonths: November to April (dry season, fewer mosquitoes); May to September for calmer snorkeling water
visitsNote: No 2024 figure turned up within the search budget. Usually roughly 0.5 to 0.7 million a year (approximate, unverified).

name: Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park
signature: The Painted Wall, Colorado's tallest cliff at about 2,250 feet, streaked with pink pegmatite
bestMonths: May to October (the North Rim and most of the South Rim road close in winter)
visitsNote: No 2024 figure turned up within the search budget. Usually roughly 300,000 to 350,000 a year (approximate, unverified).

name: Bryce Canyon National Park
signature: The hoodoos of Bryce Amphitheater, seen from Sunrise, Sunset, and Inspiration Points
bestMonths: May to June and September to October
visitsNote: From a secondary 2024 list (explorewithalec, which also shows 2023 at 2,461,269, up 1.5%). It matches the LendingTree 2024 NPS table.

name: Canyonlands National Park
signature: Mesa Arch at sunrise in the Island in the Sky district
bestMonths: April to May and September to October
visitsNote: From a secondary 2024 list (explorewithalec) that draws on NPS stats. It was not checked directly against irma.nps.gov.

name: Capitol Reef National Park
signature: The Waterpocket Fold, plus the Fruita orchards and fresh pies at the historic Gifford Homestead
bestMonths: April to June and September to October (orchard harvest season)
visitsNote: From a secondary 2024 list (explorewithalec) that draws on NPS stats. It was not checked directly against irma.nps.gov.

name: Carlsbad Caverns National Park
signature: The Big Room, an 8-acre cave chamber 750 feet underground (reached by elevator or the Natural Entrance trail)
bestMonths: May to October for the evening bat flights (peak in late summer); the cave is a steady 56°F all year
visitsNote: Only one secondary 2024 list (explorewithalec) gave this figure. Not checked against NPS directly.

name: Channel Islands National Park
signature: Painted Cave on Santa Cruz Island, one of the world's largest sea caves, plus the endemic island fox
bestMonths: March to May (wildflowers, gray whales) and September to October (calm, clear water)
visitsNote: No 2024 figure turned up within the search budget. Usually roughly 300,000 a year, much of it counted at the mainland visitor center (approximate, unverified).

name: Congaree National Park
signature: The 2.6-mile Boardwalk Loop through old-growth bottomland hardwood forest, with synchronous fireflies in May and June
bestMonths: March to May, mid-May to mid-June (fireflies), and October to November
visitsNote: No 2024 figure turned up within the search budget. Usually roughly 200,000 to 250,000 a year (approximate, unverified).

name: Crater Lake National Park
signature: Crater Lake, at 1,943 feet the deepest lake in the U.S., with Wizard Island rising inside the caldera
bestMonths: July to September (Rim Drive fully open; snow often lingers into June)
visitsNote: From a secondary 2024 list (explorewithalec). Another list (camperchamp) shows 632,242, probably a different year. Check against NPS stats.

name: Cuyahoga Valley National Park
signature: Brandywine Falls, a 65-foot waterfall, plus the Cuyahoga Valley Scenic Railroad along the Ohio & Erie Canal Towpath
bestMonths: September to October (fall color) and May to June
visitsNote: No confirmed 2024 NPS figure. One secondary list (camperchamp, updated 2026) shows 3,025,325, but its year looks inconsistent. Usually roughly 2.6 to 3 million a year (approximate).

name: Death Valley National Park
signature: Badwater Basin, 282 feet below sea level, the lowest point in North America
visitsNote: From a secondary 2024 list (explorewithalec) that draws on NPS stats. It was not checked directly against irma.nps.gov.

name: Denali National Park and Preserve
signature: North America's tallest peak (20,310 ft), plus the only NPS sled-dog kennels with working ranger huskies
bestMonths: June-August (buses run late May to mid-September)
visitsNote: Calendar-2024 figure not found within the search budget. A third-party aggregator of NPS Stats reports about 543,300 visits in calendar 2025. Acreage is the national park portion only; park plus preserve is about 6.05M acres.

name: Dry Tortugas National Park
signature: Fort Jefferson, the largest all-masonry fort in the Americas (about 16 million bricks), on a speck of island 70 miles west of Key West
visitsNote: Calendar-2024 figure not found within the search budget. A third-party aggregator of NPS Stats reports about 89,355 visits in calendar 2025. Reachable only by ferry or seaplane.

name: Everglades National Park
signature: Anhinga Trail boardwalk, where alligators sun themselves a few feet away; the only place on Earth where alligators and crocodiles live side by side
visitsNote: NPS Annual Park Ranking Report for 2024 (rank 96 among all NPS units). The FY2024 interagency report gives 743,303. Authorized in 1934 and formally established and dedicated in 1947.

name: Gates of the Arctic National Park and Preserve
signature: No roads, trails or campgrounds at all, entirely above the Arctic Circle; the granite spires of the Arrigetch Peaks
visitsNote: Least-visited national park in 2024 (NPS data via CNN). Acreage is the park portion only; park plus preserve is about 8.47M acres.

name: Gateway Arch National Park
signature: The 630-foot stainless-steel Gateway Arch, with a tram of tiny pods that rides up to the top
visitsNote: NPS Annual Park Ranking Report for 2024 (rank 38 among all NPS units). Statista also reports about 2.6M. A Wikipedia figure of about 1.16M conflicts with both. Founded as Jefferson National Expansion Memorial in 1935.

name: Glacier National Park
signature: Going-to-the-Sun Road over Logan Pass at 6,646 ft
visitsNote: Rounded: reported as about 3.20M (10th most-visited national park in 2024, up about 9% on 2023). The exact figure was not retrieved.

name: Glacier Bay National Park and Preserve
signature: Tidewater glaciers such as Margerie Glacier calving house-sized chunks of ice into the bay
visitsNote: Fiscal-year 2024 figure (October 2023 to September 2024) from the Federal Interagency recreation visitation report; the calendar-2024 figure was not retrieved. Most visitors arrive by cruise ship. Acreage is the park portion.

name: Grand Canyon National Park
signature: The mile-deep gorge cut by the Colorado River, seen from South Rim viewpoints like Mather Point
visitsNote: Rounded: reported as about 4.91M (3rd most-visited national park in 2024). The exact figure was not retrieved.

name: Grand Teton National Park
signature: The Teton Range rising about 7,000 ft straight up from the Jackson Hole valley floor, with no foothills in the way
visitsNote: Rounded: reported as about 3.62M (9th most-visited national park in 2024). The exact figure was not retrieved.

name: Great Basin National Park
signature: Ancient Great Basin bristlecone pines, some over 4,000 years old, plus the marble formations of Lehman Caves
visitsNote: Secondary source: a travel blog citing NPS 2024 data, not confirmed against NPS directly.

name: Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve
signature: Star Dune, the tallest dune in North America (about 750 ft), with Medano Creek's seasonal surge flow at its base
visitsNote: Fiscal-year 2024 figure (October 2023 to September 2024) from the Federal Interagency recreation visitation report; the calendar-2024 figure was not retrieved. Acreage is the park portion; park plus preserve is about 149,000 acres.

name: Great Smoky Mountains National Park
signature: Mist-wrapped Appalachian ridgelines seen from Clingmans Dome, plus Cades Cove's historic homesteads and wildlife loop
visitsNote: Most-visited national park in 2024, reported as 12.19M (about twice second-place Zion). The exact count is from recalled NPS Stats data, matched to that 12.19M figure.

name: Guadalupe Mountains National Park
signature: Guadalupe Peak (8,751 ft), the highest point in Texas, and the El Capitan cliff, part of a fossilized Permian reef
visitsNote: Fiscal-year 2024 figure (October 2023 to September 2024) from the Federal Interagency recreation visitation report; the calendar-2024 figure was not retrieved. Authorized in 1966 and established in 1972.

name: Haleakala National Park
signature: Sunrise from the 10,023-ft summit above a sea of clouds (reservation required)
bestMonths: Year-round; April-May and September-October are best
visitsNote: NPS Annual Park Ranking Report for 2024 (rank 100 among NPS units), matching the NPS Haleakala news release. Part of Hawaii National Park from 1916; a separate park since 1961.

name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park
signature: Kilauea's Halemaumau crater, with episodic lava fountaining in recent years
visitsNote: NPS Annual Park Ranking Report for 2024 (rank 62 among NPS units). The FY2024 interagency figure is 1,420,751.

name: Hot Springs National Park
signature: Bathhouse Row's historic bathhouses, fed by 143°F thermal spring water; Buckstaff Bathhouse has operated since 1912
visitsNote: NPS Annual Park Ranking Report for 2024 (rank 42 among NPS units). Hot Springs Reservation dates to 1832; it became a national park in 1921.

name: Indiana Dunes National Park
visitsNote: Calendar-year 2024 recreation visits per NPS IRMA figures reproduced in 2024 ranking lists; some sites mislabel a lower 2025 figure (2,629,497) as 2024.
signature: Towering sand dunes on the Lake Michigan shoreline, best experienced on the 3 Dune Challenge at West Beach

name: Isle Royale National Park
visitsNote: 2024 recreation visits per Smithsonian's ranking of NPS 2024 data.
signature: Roadless Lake Superior island home to the world's longest-running predator-prey study of wolves and moose (since 1958)

name: Joshua Tree National Park
visitsNote: Calendar-year 2024 recreation visits per NPS-sourced 2024 ranking lists (just under 3 million).
signature: Spiky Joshua trees among giant stacked granite boulder piles at Hidden Valley

name: Katmai National Park and Preserve
visitsNote: 2024 recreation visits per Smithsonian's ranking of NPS 2024 data. Acreage is park plus preserve.
signature: Brown bears snatching leaping sockeye salmon at Brooks Falls (home of Fat Bear Week)

name: Kenai Fjords National Park
visitsNote: Calendar-year 2024 recreation visits per an NPS-sourced 2024 ranking list; not confirmed in a second source.
signature: Exit Glacier, a road-accessible arm of the 700-square-mile Harding Icefield

name: Kings Canyon National Park
visitsNote: Calendar-year 2024 recreation visits per an NPS-sourced 2024 ranking list; not confirmed in a second source.
signature: The General Grant Tree, a giant sequoia designated the Nation's Christmas Tree

name: Kobuk Valley National Park
visitsNote: 2024 recreation visits per Smithsonian/CNN rankings of NPS 2024 data (third-least-visited park).
signature: The Great Kobuk Sand Dunes, about 25 square miles of dunes above the Arctic Circle

name: Lake Clark National Park and Preserve
visitsNote: 2024 recreation visits per Smithsonian's ranking of NPS 2024 data; Outdoors.com reports 19,395, so treat as approximate. Acreage is park plus preserve.
signature: Richard Proenneke's hand-built log cabin on Twin Lakes beneath volcanic peaks

name: Lassen Volcanic National Park
visitsNote: Calendar-year 2024 figure from an NPS-sourced ranking list; the federal FY2024 interagency report lists 362,638 (fiscal year).
signature: Bumpass Hell, a boardwalk through boiling mud pots and steaming fumaroles

name: Mammoth Cave National Park
visitsNote: Calendar-year 2024 recreation visits per ranking list and Wikipedia; FY2024 interagency report lists 739,006.
signature: The world's longest known cave system, with more than 400 miles mapped

name: Mesa Verde National Park
visitsNote: Calendar-year 2024 figure from an NPS-sourced ranking list; FY2024 interagency report lists 488,311.
signature: Cliff Palace, the largest cliff dwelling in North America

name: Mount Rainier National Park
visitsNote: Calendar-year 2024 recreation visits per NPS-sourced 2024 ranking lists.
signature: Paradise wildflower meadows beneath the 14,410-foot glacier-wrapped volcano

name: New River Gorge National Park and Preserve
visitsNote: Record 2024 recreation visits, up 6.31% from 1,707,223 in 2023, per NPS data reported by WVVA and WCHS. Acreage is park plus preserve.
signature: New River Gorge Bridge, a 3,030-foot steel arch 876 feet above the river
bestMonths: May-October (mid-October for foliage and Bridge Day)

name: North Cascades National Park
visitsNote: 2024 recreation visits per Smithsonian/CNN rankings of NPS 2024 data (second-least-visited park). Count covers the national park unit only, not the adjacent Ross Lake and Lake Chelan recreation areas.
signature: More than 300 glaciers, the most of any U.S. park outside Alaska, above turquoise Diablo Lake

name: Olympic National Park
visitsNote: Rounded: 2024 rankings report about 3.72 million recreation visits (8th most visited), up roughly 27% from about 2.9 million in 2023. Exact count not confirmed.
signature: The moss-draped Hall of Mosses in the Hoh Rain Forest

name: Petrified Forest National Park
visitsNote: Calendar-year 2024 figure from an NPS-sourced ranking list; FY2024 interagency report lists 554,160.
signature: Rainbow-hued petrified logs about 218 million years old at Crystal Forest and Blue Mesa

name: Pinnacles National Park
signature: Bear Gulch talus cave, a flashlight-required passage under fallen boulders, with California condors circling the volcanic spires above
visitsNote: 2024 recreation visits not found in available searches.

name: Redwood National and State Parks
signature: Old-growth coast redwoods, including Hyperion (about 380 ft), the tallest known living tree on Earth
visitsNote: 2024 figure not found in available searches. NPS counts cover the jointly managed national and state park lands.

name: Rocky Mountain National Park
signature: Trail Ridge Road, the highest continuous paved road in the U.S., topping out at 12,183 ft
bestMonths: Late June-September (Trail Ridge Road open); September-early October for elk rut and aspens
visitsNote: About 4.15 million (rounded), per National Parks Traveler citing NPS 2024 data; 18th among all NPS units and 5th among national parks.

name: Saguaro National Park
signature: Forests of giant saguaro cacti, which grow naturally only in the Sonoran Desert and can top 40 ft
visitsNote: 2024 figure not verified. NPS 2023 annual ranking listed 1,010,906; one secondary listing shows 847,749, but its year is unclear.

name: Sequoia National Park
signature: General Sherman Tree, the largest living tree on Earth by volume (about 52,500 cubic feet)
visitsNote: 2024 figure not verified. NPS 2023 annual ranking listed 980,567; one secondary listing shows 1,378,337, but its year is unclear.

name: Shenandoah National Park
signature: Skyline Drive, 105 miles along the Blue Ridge with about 75 scenic overlooks
visitsNote: 2024 figure not found in available searches; recent years typically run around 1.4-1.6 million recreation visits.

name: Theodore Roosevelt National Park
signature: Free-roaming wild horses and bison in the South Unit badlands near Medora
bestMonths: May-September (June for wildflowers and bison calves)
visitsNote: 2024 figure not verified. NPS 2023 annual ranking listed 746,862; one secondary listing shows 729,893, possibly 2024 but unconfirmed.

name: Virgin Islands National Park
signature: Trunk Bay's underwater snorkel trail, with signs on the seafloor
bestMonths: December-April (dry season; hurricane season runs June-November)
visitsNote: 2024 figure not verified. NPS 2023 annual ranking listed 343,685; one secondary listing shows 471,074, but its year is unclear.

name: Voyageurs National Park
signature: A boat-access park: about 40 percent water, spread across Rainy, Kabetogama, Namakan and Sand Point lakes and 500-plus islands
visitsNote: 2024 recreation visits not found in available searches.

name: White Sands National Park
signature: Most of the world's largest gypsum dunefield (about 275 square miles in all), with white dunes you can sled down
visitsNote: 2024 figure not verified. NPS 2023 annual ranking listed 729,096; one secondary listing shows 659,742, but its year is unclear.

name: Wind Cave National Park
signature: Boxwork, the honeycomb-like calcite formation; Wind Cave holds an estimated 95 percent of the world's known boxwork
bestMonths: May-October above ground; cave tours run year-round at a steady 54F
visitsNote: 2024 recreation visits not found in available searches.

name: Wrangell-St. Elias National Park and Preserve
signature: Kennecott's red 14-story copper concentration mill, at the end of the 60-mile gravel McCarthy Road
visitsNote: 2024 recreation visits not found in available searches. The acreage counts the national park only; with the preserve the total is about 13.2 million acres.

name: Yellowstone National Park
signature: Old Faithful, in a park that holds roughly half of the world's active geysers
visitsNote: Coverage of NPS 2024 data confirms about 4.7 million (4th among national parks). The exact count matches Yellowstone's reported 2024 total but was recalled, not directly verified in search.

name: Yosemite National Park
signature: El Capitan, a sheer granite monolith about 3,000 ft tall above Yosemite Valley
visitsNote: About 4.12 million (rounded), per National Parks Traveler citing NPS 2024 data; 20th among all NPS units and 6th among national parks.

name: Zion National Park
signature: The Narrows, a hike up the Virgin River between canyon walls up to about 1,000 ft high
visitsNote: 4,946,592 recreation visits per Smithsonian citing NPS; the 2nd most-visited national park in 2024.
